chunks: That is how We have made for each apostle opponents, the satans among men and jinns, who inspire one another with deceitful talk. But if your Lord had willed they would not have done so. Pay no attention to them and to what they fabricate.
ai.seo_question: Who are the satans of men and jinn mentioned in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the cosmic reality that every prophet faces opposition from both jinn and humans, specifically those who are 'shayatin' (devils) in their respective realms. The 'flowery speech' (zakhraf al-qawl) refers to the persuasive but deceptive rhetoric used to mislead followers, illustrating the spiritual warfare inherent in prophetic missions. The command to 'leave them' implies a strategic patience and detachment rather than immediate destruction, acknowledging divine wisdom in allowing this adversarial dynamic to persist.
